storage.page.title: Storage Locations and Usage
storage.page.partial: A folder was too big to measure completely. Sizes marked + are at least this much.
storage.page.intro: The prompt cache lives on Anthropic's servers and takes no space on this computer. What does take space, and gets written again and again, is transcripts, file backups, plugins and logs.
storage.page.neverRuns: Agent Monitor only writes these commands; it never runs them. Open in Terminal types the command without pressing Enter, so you can check it first.
storage.page.footer: Sizes are measured only while this page is open, at most once every 10 minutes unless you press Refresh.
storage.btn.terminal.tip: Types the command into a new terminal without pressing Enter. Check it, then press Enter yourself.

storage.retention.label: Transcripts kept for
storage.retention.tip: When it starts, Claude Code deletes transcripts older than this. Change it with cleanupPeriodDays in {path}. Starting Claude Code with --no-session-persistence writes no transcript at all, and Agent Monitor can't see that session.

storage.mig.heading: Move data to another disk
storage.mig.why: The real problem is free space on the system disk. Moving these folders frees space there; it doesn't reduce the memory each session process uses.
storage.mig.suggested: Suggested: the disk with the most free space
storage.mig.toHint: If the folder you choose isn't called “{app}”, the data goes into a new “{app}” folder inside it.
storage.mig.noTarget: No other writable disk found. Choose a folder on another disk.

storage.mig.planA.win: A · Move {sub} only, with a directory junction
storage.mig.planA.desc: Copies {sub}, the biggest folder, to the destination and leaves a link at the old path. {app} keeps using the same path, so nothing else needs to change.
storage.mig.planB.desc: Copies the whole data folder, settings and plugins included, and points {name} at the new place.
storage.mig.nothing: There's no {sub} folder yet, so there's nothing to move.
storage.mig.linked: Already moved: {sub} is a link to {target}.

storage.step.close.codex: Wait until Codex has finished every turn, and don't start a new one while moving.

storage.step.cleanup: When everything works, delete the backup:
storage.step.rollback: To undo (copies anything new back to the original first):

storage.step.envShell: For Claude Code in a terminal, add this line to your shell profile (for example ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc):
storage.step.envShell.codex: Add this line to your shell profile (for example ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc):

storage.step.monitor: Point Agent Monitor at the new place (user settings):

storage.plan.note.symlink: {name} is copied to the destination, the original is renamed {bak}, and a link with the old name points to the new place.
storage.plan.note.rsync: rsync -a keeps timestamps and permissions. The original is renamed only after the copy succeeds.
storage.plan.note.junction: robocopy copies the folder, then mklink /J creates a directory junction. No administrator rights are needed; the destination must be a local drive. The command runs in PowerShell.
storage.plan.note.noRsync: If rsync isn't installed, install it, or replace that step with cp -a.
storage.plan.note.guard: The command checks first and changes nothing if the folder is already a link or a .bak copy already exists.
storage.plan.note.env.copy: The folder is copied and the original is renamed .bak. Nothing uses the new place until {name} is set.
storage.plan.note.env.claude: Claude Code reads {name} when it starts. In VS Code, set it with the Claude Code extension setting claudeCode.environmentVariables. Don't put it in Claude's settings.json: that file lives inside the folder being moved.
storage.plan.note.env.claudeJson: With CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set, Claude Code keeps .claude.json inside that folder, so the command copies ~/.claude.json there too.
storage.plan.note.env.login: You may need to sign in again after switching (not verified).
storage.plan.note.env.codex: Codex reads {name} when it starts. The Codex extension has no setting for environment variables, so set it in your shell profile and restart VS Code (not verified for the Codex desktop app).
storage.plan.note.env.monitor: Agent Monitor can't see environment variables that are set only for Claude Code or Codex, so it needs its own setting to follow the move.
storage.plan.error.BAD_PATH: The path contains characters that can't go into a command.
storage.plan.error.SAME_PATH: The destination is the folder being moved.
storage.plan.error.TARGET_INSIDE_SOURCE: The destination can't be inside the folder being moved.
storage.plan.error.SOURCE_INSIDE_TARGET: The destination can't contain the folder being moved.
storage.target.sameDisk: This destination is on the same disk as the data now, so moving there frees no space.
storage.target.synced: This looks like a synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive). Constant writes conflict with syncing, so choose another folder.
storage.target.notMounted: {path} isn't available. Is the drive connected?
storage.target.notEmpty: {path} already has files in it. The copy will merge with them.
storage.target.noSpace: Not enough free space: needs about {need}, {free} free.
storage.live.claude: These Claude Code sessions are open ({n}). Close them before moving:
storage.live.codex: Codex is still working in these sessions ({n}). Wait for them to finish before moving:
storage.live.confirm: {app} sessions are still open ({n}). Moving data while they write can lose or damage transcripts. Close them first.
storage.notes.heading: Before you move anything
storage.note.mount: The external drive must be connected before you start Claude Code or Codex. Otherwise the link points nowhere: sessions fail to save, or start over in a new empty folder.
storage.note.sync: Don't use a synced folder such as iCloud Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive. Constant writes conflict with syncing.
storage.note.noSessions: Don't run any session while moving.
storage.note.keepBak: Keep the .bak copy until you're sure everything works.
storage.note.windows: On Windows, use a directory junction (mklink /J) instead of a symbolic link. Agent Monitor on Windows shows those commands.
storage.note.windows.here: On Windows the commands use a directory junction (mklink /J) and run in PowerShell.
storage.note.memory: Moving data frees disk space only. It doesn't reduce the memory each session process uses.
